CS 2223.name: Algorithms
CS 2223.description: Develops algorithm design and analysis through greedy, recursive, dynamic, heuristic and probabilistic methods, using sorting, graphs and string problems.

review.rationale: Algorithm design and worst/average-case analysis establish foundational computer science.

MA 2611.name: Applied Statistics I
MA 2611.description: Introduces applied statistical analysis through study design, data exploration, estimation and hypothesis tests using real datasets and software.

review.rationale: Statistical inference and study design are the central methods, despite practical industrial/scientific examples.

MA 2612.name: Applied Statistics II
MA 2612.description: Continues applied statistics with regression, categorical-data tables, experimental analysis and distribution-free methods.

review.rationale: The complete description develops statistical methods rather than an unspecified data-science survey.

DS 1010.name: Data Science I: Introduction to Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
DS 1010.description: Introduces data preparation, programming, statistics, learning methods, visualization and responsible AI through projects with real datasets.

review.rationale: The broad introduction deliberately spans programming, mathematical analysis and AI methods without establishing one dominant subject.

DS 2010.name: Data Science II: Statistical Modeling and Analysis
DS 2010.recommended_background: Data science basics equivalent to DS 1010 , applied statistics and regression equivalent to MA 2611 and MA 2612 , and the ability to write computer programs in a scientific language equivalent to a CS programming course at the CS 1000 or CS 2000 level are assumed.
DS 2010.description: Develops prediction and inference workflows with regression, classification, decision trees, dimensionality reduction, feature engineering and bias-variance analysis.

review.rationale: After a brief mathematics review, the description explicitly centers introductory machine-learning methods and predictive data workflows.

DS 3010.name: Data Science III: Computational Methods
DS 3010.recommended_background: Data science basics equivalent to DS 1010 , and data analysis principles and modeling equivalent to DS 2010 , knowledge of basic statistics equivalent to ( MA 2611 and MA 2612 ), and the ability to program equivalent to ( CS 1004 or CS 1101 or CS 1102 ) and ( CS 2102 , CS 2103 or CS 2119 ), as well as understanding of databases equivalent to ( CS 3431 or MIS 3720 ) are assumed.
DS 3010.description: Develops large-data workflows spanning API collection, data management, cloud infrastructure and machine/deep-learning toolkits.

review.rationale: The stated pipeline combines data infrastructure and AI toolkits without a dominant single subject; it is not mathematics merely from the older title-only candidate list.

FIN 2070.name: Risk Analysis for Decision Making
FIN 2070.description: Introduces financial decisions through valuation, interest rates, investment risk and returns, establishing financial literacy for further study.

review.rationale: The actual description concerns substantive finance and valuation, not generic decision-theory mathematics or AI.

MA 1021.name: Calculus I
MA 1021.recommended_background: Algebra, trigonometry and analytic geometry. Although the course will make use of computers, no programming experience is assumed.
MA 1021.description: Introduces single-variable derivatives, limits, continuity, approximation and optimization.

review.rationale: Differential calculus methods define the subject.

MA 1021.credit_restriction: Credit may not be earned for both MA1021 and MA1020.

MA 1022.name: Calculus II
MA 1022.recommended_background: MA 1020 or MA 1021 . Although the course will make use of computers, no programming experience is assumed.
MA 1022.description: Develops integration, its foundational theorem, computational techniques and geometric or engineering applications.

review.rationale: Integral calculus remains central despite engineering examples.

MA 2071.name: Matrices and Linear Algebra I
MA 2071.recommended_background: None, although basic knowledge of equations for planes and lines in space would be helpful.
MA 2071.description: Introduces matrices, linear equations, transformations, eigenvalues, vector spaces and numerical linear-algebra methods.

review.rationale: The description explicitly develops linear-algebra theory and techniques.

MA 2071.credit_restriction: Credit may not be earned for both MA2071 and MA2072.

MA 2072.name: Accelerated Matrices and Linear Algebra I
MA 2072.description: Accelerates linear algebra through vector spaces, eigenvalues, least squares and singular-value methods, with computational examples.

review.rationale: Matrix and vector-space theory organize the data-science applications.

MA 2072.credit_restriction: Credit may not be earned for both MA2072 and MA2071.

MA 2073.name: Matrices and Linear Algebra II
MA 2073.description: Deepens linear algebra through abstract spaces, transformations, polynomials, diagonalization and matrix exponentials.

review.rationale: Advanced linear-algebra theory is explicit.

CS 1004.name: Introduction to Programming for Non-Majors
CS 1004.recommended_background: None. All Computer Science students and other students wishing to prepare for 3000-level courses in Computer Science should take CS 1101 / CS 1102 instead of CS 1004 . This course provides sufficient background for CS 2301 Systems Programming for Non-Majors.
CS 1004.description: Introduces imperative and scripting programs, control flow, decomposition, basic structures, testing and data/device interfaces.

review.rationale: Programming construction and debugging are central.

CS 1101.name: Introduction to Program Design
CS 1101.recommended_background: None. Either CS 1101 or CS 1102 provides sufficient background for further courses in the CS department. Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both this course and CS 1102 .
CS 1101.description: Develops functional program design using structured data, recursion, higher-order functions and testing.

review.rationale: General program design and implementation establish foundational computer science.

CS 1101.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both CS1101 and CS1102.

CS 1102.name: Accelerated Introduction to Program Design
CS 1102.recommended_background: Substantial prior programming experience (including functions, recursion, and lists, as would be covered in high-school Advanced Placement Computer Science A courses, but not necessarily AP CS Principles courses). Either CS 1101 or CS 1102 provides sufficient background for further courses in the CS department. Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both this course and CS 1101 .
CS 1102.description: Combines accelerated functional programming with selected advanced programming topics and an individual project.

review.rationale: The entire course remains focused on program construction, despite examples involving web protocols and languages.

CS 1102.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both CS1102 and CS1101.

OBC 1010.name: Leadership Practice
OBC 1010.description: Examines leadership through self-awareness, communication, cultural differences, ethics and contemporary organizational challenges.

review.rationale: Human relationships, communication and ethical leadership organize the complete description.

ACC 2060.name: Financial Statements for Decision Making
ACC 2060.description: Uses financial statements, accounting concepts and sensitivity analysis to support business decisions and assess stakeholder impacts.

review.rationale: Substantive accounting and financial-statement interpretation are the domain.

OIE 2850.name: Engineering Economics
OIE 2850.description: Evaluates engineering alternatives through financial value, cash flow, tax, inflation, uncertainty and replacement decisions.

review.rationale: Engineering economics and financial decisions establish applied domain knowledge; arithmetic does not alone imply a mathematics course.

MKT 4030.name: Marketing Strategy
MKT 4030.description: Develops marketing strategies from customer insights, segmentation, competitive analysis and market conditions.

review.rationale: Strategic marketing practice is the dominant domain.

BUS 1020.name: Global Environment of Business Decisions
BUS 1020.description: Examines global business environments through trade, culture, political risk, financial systems, law and supply chains.

review.rationale: The description integrates social/political/cultural analysis with business-domain decisions without a clearly dominant taxonomy subject.

BUS 2020.name: The Legal Environment of Business Decisions
BUS 2020.description: Examines contracts, torts, intellectual property and organizational law in technology and global business decisions.

review.rationale: Legal interpretation is central, despite business examples.

ETR 2900.name: Social Entrepreneurship
ETR 2900.recommended_background: Familiarity with concepts of creativity, innovation, entrepreneurial and critical thinking, ethics, cross-cultural relations, and social problems ( OBC 1010 , BUS 1020 , ACC 2060 or equivalent).
ETR 2900.description: Develops social-enterprise models, opportunity assessment, impact evaluation, organizational structures and financing.

review.rationale: Entrepreneurship tools and operation of social ventures organize the social-problem context.

ETR 2900.offering_note: The description says this course is offered in academic years ending in even numbers; this is not a guarantee of a particular term offering.

ETR 4930.name: Growing and Managing New Ventures
ETR 4930.description: Examines how ventures expand markets, plan products, manage operations and sustain cash flow as they grow.

review.rationale: New-venture management is substantive business practice.

OBC 4367.name: Leadership, Ethics, and Social Responsibility
OBC 4367.description: Investigates ethical leadership, corporate governance and social responsibility through reflection and organizational cases.

review.rationale: Ethics and social responsibility are the explicit central subjects.

CS 3431.name: Database Systems I
CS 3431.recommended_background: CS 2022 and either CS 2102 , CS 2103 , or CS 2119 .
CS 3431.description: Develops relational databases through models, queries, design theory, data independence and implementation.

review.rationale: Database systems and storage/design abstractions establish systems content.

CS 3431.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both CS3431 and CS542.

CS 4433/DS 4433.name: Big Data Management and Analytics
CS 4433/DS 4433.recommended_background: Knowledge in database systems at the level of CS 4432 , and programming experience are assumed.
CS 4433/DS 4433.description: Studies distributed data infrastructure, streaming, cloud platforms, query optimization and scalable analytics through projects.

review.rationale: Distributed database infrastructure, storage and query processing dominate the analytics context.

MIS 2300.name: Business Applications of Blockchain
MIS 2300.recommended_background: Basic knowledge of programming (Equivalent to CS 1004 or other introductory programming courses)
MIS 2300.description: Studies blockchain operation, smart contracts, business applications, implementation projects and regulatory challenges.

review.rationale: Computing infrastructure and business application practice both receive explicit attention; neither clearly dominates.

MIS 3720.name: Business Data Management
MIS 3720.recommended_background: Some programming knowledge (e.g., CS 1004 , CS 2119 , OIE 2600 or equivalent knowledge)
MIS 3720.description: Designs and implements business databases using relational models, queries, normalization and concurrency/recovery techniques.

review.rationale: The description teaches database mechanisms and design, not merely business use of software.

BUS 2080.name: Data Analysis for Decision Making
BUS 2080.recommended_background: Basic statistics, equivalent to that in MA 2611 and MA 2612 .
BUS 2080.description: Uses business analytics and advanced spreadsheets to support forecasting, operations and customer-related decisions.

review.rationale: Business decision practice organizes the data techniques; no specific AI-method focus is established.

OIE 2081.name: Introduction to Prescriptive Analytics
OIE 2081.recommended_background: Basic statistics, equivalent to that in MA 2611 and MA 2612 .
OIE 2081.description: Introduces optimization and simulation for selecting actions across varied engineering and management problems.

review.rationale: Mathematical optimization and simulation are the transferable central methods across the example domains.

FIN 3330.name: Financial Analytics
FIN 3330.description: Develops predictive financial-data models using clustering, classification, regression, regularization and validation in R.

review.rationale: The stated objective and detailed topics center modern machine-learning methods; financial problems supply the application data.

MKT 4040.name: Marketing Analytics
MKT 4040.recommended_background: Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) and Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).
MKT 4040.description: Applies marketing analytics to segmentation, churn, pricing and customer value in business cases.

review.rationale: Marketing decision practice dominates; analytics terminology alone does not establish an AI-method course.

OIE 3020.name: Achieving Effective Operations
OIE 3020.description: Analyzes and implements operating processes amid resource, stakeholder, sustainability and ethical constraints.

review.rationale: Operational process management and practical improvement are the substantive domain.

MIS 4084.name: Business Intelligence
MIS 4084.recommended_background: Previous knowledge in data management, such as that provided by MIS 3720 Business Data Management or CS 3431 Database Systems I.
MIS 4084.description: Uses business-intelligence software and case analysis to turn organizational data into recommendations.

review.rationale: Business decision support through existing tools is central, rather than computing infrastructure or explicit AI methods.

MKT 2620.name: Marketing Research
MKT 2620.recommended_background: Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) and Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).
MKT 2620.description: Develops marketing research from problem formulation through study design, data collection and communication of findings.

review.rationale: Research methods serve explicit marketing decisions and domain practice.

MKT 2630.name: Sales Management and Analytics
MKT 2630.recommended_background: Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) + Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).
MKT 2630.description: Combines sales strategy, employee management, negotiation and data analysis to align selling with organizational goals.

review.rationale: Sales management and professional selling are the primary applied domain.

MKT 2640.name: Consumer Behavior and Analytics
MKT 2640.recommended_background: Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).
MKT 2640.description: Uses consumer theories and market data to inform segmentation, branding, pricing and other marketing decisions.

review.rationale: Psychological and social theories support practical consumer/marketing analysis; the business domain remains dominant.

MKT 2640.credit_restriction: Credit may not be earned for both MKT2640 and MKT3650.

MKT 3620.name: E-Commerce and Web Analytics
MKT 3620.recommended_background: Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) and Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).
MKT 3620.description: Uses web-performance measures, search strategies and customer targeting to improve digital-commerce decisions.

review.rationale: Digital commerce and marketing effectiveness are the practical domain, not systems engineering.

MKT 3630.name: Digital and Social Media Marketing Analytics
MKT 3630.recommended_background: Foundational knowledge in Marketing or Consumer Behavior (equivalent to MKT 1100 or MKT 2640 ) and Knowledge of Statistics (equivalent to that in MA 2611 or MA 2612 ).
MKT 3630.description: Examines digital-media analytics for marketing mix, branding, communication and customer relationships.

review.rationale: The course centers marketing management and brand practice rather than general data-science methods.

OIE 3460.name: Simulation Modeling and Analysis
OIE 3460.description: Develops simulation experiments and statistical interpretation using queueing, inventory and industrial examples.

review.rationale: Simulation methodology, experimental design and statistical analysis organize the domain examples.

OIE 3510.name: Stochastic Models
OIE 3510.recommended_background: Knowledge of calculus and introductory probability and statistics.
OIE 3510.description: Develops risk-based decisions with stochastic models including Markov chains, Poisson processes and queues.

review.rationale: Probability models and quantitative risk methods are the central subject.

OIE 4430.name: Advanced Prescriptive Analytics: From Data to Impact
OIE 4430.recommended_background: An introductory level of exposure to prescriptive analytics or linear optimization, such as can be found in OIE 2081 , MA 2210 , or MA 3231 .
OIE 4430.description: Formulates and solves advanced optimization problems with integer variables, nonlinear relationships and uncertainty.

review.rationale: Mathematical model formulation and solution methods dominate the varied practical examples.

OIE 4430.suggested_background: Note the mathematical foundations of some of the optimization techniques in this class are in MA 3231 . Students might also benefit from MA 3233 .
OIE 4430.credit_restriction: Credit may not be earned for both OIE4430 and OIE4420.

ETR 1100.name: Engineering Innovation and Entrepreneurship
ETR 1100.description: Examines commercial aspects of engineering innovation and how new products and ventures develop.

review.rationale: Entrepreneurship and commercialization establish the applied business domain.

MIS 3010.name: Creating Value Through Innovation
MIS 3010.description: Evaluates innovations through customers, organizational capabilities, competitors and ethical or financial value.

review.rationale: Innovation assessment and commercialization are substantive business practice.

HU 3900.name: Inquiry Seminar in Humanities and Arts
HU 3900.description: Culminating humanities and arts inquiry develops communication, critical thinking and engagement with diverse perspectives through an instructor-defined theme.

review.rationale: The complete description explicitly centers communication, critical inquiry and appreciation of diverse perspectives in humanities/arts; thematic variability does not imply a technical AI subject.

HU 3900.description_prerequisites: Before enrollment, complete five Humanities and Arts courses, with at least two thematically related and at least one at the 2000 level or above.
HU 3900.eligibility_note: The course-entry minimum of two thematically related prior courses is separate from the degree policy requiring three in the depth sequence. Both can apply; the stricter graduation requirement is not waived.

HU 3910.name: Practicum in Humanities and Arts
HU 3910.description: Culminating humanities and arts inquiry develops communication, critical thinking and engagement with diverse perspectives through an instructor-defined theme.

review.rationale: The complete description explicitly centers communication, critical inquiry and appreciation of diverse perspectives in humanities/arts; thematic variability does not imply a technical AI subject.

HU 3910.description_prerequisites: Before enrollment, complete five Humanities and Arts courses, with at least two thematically related and at least one at the 2000 level or above. Instructor consent is also required.
HU 3910.eligibility_note: The course-entry minimum of two thematically related prior courses is separate from the degree policy requiring three in the depth sequence. Both can apply; the stricter graduation requirement is not waived.

CS 2119.name: Application Building with Object-Oriented Concepts
CS 2119.recommended_background: Programming experience such as found in CS 1101 , CS 1102 , CS 1004 , or CS 1005 .
CS 2119.description: Develops object-oriented applications through design, implementation and debugging, with interfaces and database access.

review.rationale: General software construction and object-oriented programming are the central subject.

CS 2119.audience_note: The description addresses non-CS majors with prior programming experience; the separate background field supplies advisory examples.

CS 4341.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
CS 4341.recommended_background: CS 2102 or CS 2103 ; CS 2223 ; and CS 3133 .
CS 4341.description: Develops AI representation, search, planning and language understanding through computational problem-solving projects.

review.rationale: Explicit AI methods and search-based problem solving define the course.

CS 4341.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both CS4341 and CS534.

MIS 3730.name: Artificial Intelligence with Business Application
MIS 3730.description: Develops AI knowledge representation, search, planning and language understanding through problem-solving projects.

review.rationale: The actual description teaches AI methods; the business-oriented title does not reduce it to general business applications.

CS 4342.name: Machine Learning
CS 4342.recommended_background: Multivariate Calculus ( MA 1024 or MA 1034 ), Linear Algebra (such as MA 2071 ), Probability ( MA 2621 or MA 2631 ), and Algorithms ( CS 2223 ). Students may not earn credit for both CS 453X and CS 4342 . Undergraduate credit may not be earned both for this course and for CS 539.
CS 4342.description: Explores theoretical and practical learning algorithms for prediction, representation, clustering and probabilistic modeling.

review.rationale: Machine-learning algorithms are explicit throughout the complete description.

CS 4342.credit_restriction: Credit may not be earned for both CS453X and CS4342. Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both CS4342 and CS539.

MIS 3787.name: Business Applications of Machine Learning
MIS 3787.description: Applies supervised and automated machine-learning tools to prediction problems across several business domains.

review.rationale: The course explicitly develops machine-learning approaches across varied applications, rather than teaching one business domain alone.

CS 1005.name: Programming for Engineers
CS 1005.recommended_background: None. Computer Science majors and other students wishing to prepare for 3000-level courses in Computer Science should take CS 1101 / CS 1102 instead of CS 1005. This course provides sufficient background for CS 2301 Systems Programming for Non-Majors . Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both this course and CS 1004. Undergraduate credit may not be earned for both this course and RBE 100X.
CS 1005.description: Introduces programming through engineered devices, using control flow, data structures, modular design, state machines and event-driven input/output. Students implement and debug reusable programs.

review.rationale: Programming and program construction are central; robotics supplies examples rather than an AI methods focus.

CS 1005.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit cannot be earned for both CS1005 and CS1004, or both CS1005 and RBE100X.
CS 1005.audience_note: CS majors and students preparing for upper-level CS are directed to CS1101/1102 instead. Provides preparation for RBE1001 and CS2301; this is not an added degree obligation.

CS 2102.name: Object-Oriented Design Concepts
CS 2102.description: Develops object-oriented program design through classes, inheritance, interfaces, exceptions, contracts and reusable patterns, with implementation and debugging exercises.

review.rationale: General software design and data-structure implementation establish computing foundations.

CS 2103.name: Accelerated Object-Oriented Design Concepts
CS 2103.recommended_background: CS 1101 or CS 1102 and significant prior experience writing object-oriented programs from scratch.
CS 2103.description: Covers object-oriented design and data structures at an accelerated pace for experienced programmers, emphasizing design critique, correctness, testing and algorithmic reasoning.

review.rationale: Advanced preparation changes pace, not the foundational software-design subject.

CS 2103.credit_restriction: Credit is available for only one of CS2102, CS2103 and CS210X.
CS 2103.audience_note: Intended for substantial prior object-oriented programming experience; AP CS A is described as sufficient, while AP CS Principles or gentler Java preparation is directed to CS2102.

MA 1020.name: Calculus I with Preliminary Topics
MA 1020.description: Combines algebra and trigonometry review with limits, differentiation and derivative applications in a fourteen-week first-calculus course.

review.rationale: Calculus and preparatory mathematical techniques determine the subject; semester duration does not alter its stated unit value.

MA 1020.credit_restriction: Credit is not available for both MA1020 and MA1021.

MA 1120.name: Calculus II (Semester Version)
MA 1120.recommended_background: MA 1020 or MA 1021 . Although the course will make use of computers, no programming experience is assumed. Students may not receive credit for both MA 1120 and MA 1022 .
MA 1120.description: Develops integral calculus, integration techniques and applications over fourteen weeks, with introductory sequence and series material.

review.rationale: Integration and mathematical analysis are central, despite engineering examples.

MA 1120.credit_restriction: Credit is not available for both MA1120 and MA1022.

CS 4343/DS 4343.name: Deep Learning
CS 4343/DS 4343.recommended_background: Machine Learning ( CS 4342 ), and knowledge of Linear Algebra (such as MA 2071 ) and Algorithms (such as CS 2223 )
CS 4343/DS 4343.description: Studies neural-network architectures, optimization and regularization, combining mathematical foundations with training networks for practical tasks.

review.rationale: Neural learning methods and their training algorithms are the explicit central subject.

CS 4445.name: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery in Databases
CS 4445.recommended_background: MA 2611 , CS 2223 , and CS 3431 or CS 3733 .
CS 4445.description: Examines discovery of patterns in large datasets through data integration and warehousing, learning and mining algorithms, and visualization.

review.rationale: The description combines substantive database integration and storage with learning-based pattern discovery; neither receives an unambiguous primary allocation.

CS 4445.offering_note: Source states offering in academic years ending in even numbers; no specific term is inferred.

DS 4635/MA 4635.name: Data Analytics and Statistical Learning
DS 4635/MA 4635.recommended_background: Linear Algebra ( MA 2071 or equivalent), Applied Statistics and Regression ( MA 2612 or equivalent), Probability ( MA 2631 or equivalent). The ability to write computer programs in a scientific language is assumed.
DS 4635/MA 4635.description: Develops statistical learning for prediction and inference through regression, classification, clustering, resampling and decision trees.

review.rationale: The explicit focus is statistical learning and predictive modeling, supporting AI/ML rather than a classification from its mathematics affiliation.

DS 4635/MA 4635.credit_restriction: Credit is not available for both MA463X and MA4635.

CS 3041.name: Human-Computer Interaction
CS 3041.description: Examines interactive systems through usability evaluation, psychological considerations, interface and hardware design, and practical development or experimental projects.

review.rationale: The complete description combines human interaction and evaluation with software/interface construction; no single taxonomy category clearly dominates.

CS 4345/DS 4345.name: Multi-Agent Systems
CS 4345/DS 4345.recommended_background: Basic knowledge of linear algebra, probability theory, and Python programming. Familiarity with machine learning and deep learning equivalent to ( DS 3010 , CS 4445 , CS 4342 ). Familiarity with deep learning equivalent to CS/DS 4343 encouraged.
CS 4345/DS 4345.description: Explores autonomous-agent coordination, communication and decision-making, including cooperative and competitive settings and contemporary learning methods.

review.rationale: Intelligent multi-agent decision algorithms and AI enhancements are the explicit central subject.

CS 3043/SS 3043.name: Social Implications of Information Processing
CS 3043/SS 3043.recommended_background: A general knowledge of computers and computer systems.
CS 3043/SS 3043.description: Examines social, ethical and philosophical effects of computing, human-machine relationships, and governance of computer-based systems.

review.rationale: Social consequences, ethics and governance establish human context independently of the degree ethics slot.

CS 3043/SS 3043.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit is not available for both this course and CS505.
CS 3043/SS 3043.eligibility_note: Cannot satisfy the WPI Social Science Requirement; its major ethics eligibility does not waive this separate exclusion.

CS 3733.name: Software Engineering
CS 3733.description: Develops software-engineering practice across requirements, design, implementation, testing, configuration and project management through a substantial project.

review.rationale: General software construction and lifecycle methods establish foundations, rather than infrastructure operation.

CS 3733.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit is not available for both CS3733 and CS509.

CS 4344/DS 4344.name: Natural Language Processing: From Foundations to Large Language Models
CS 4344/DS 4344.recommended_background: Programming skills equivalent to ( CS 1004 or CS 1101 or CS 1102 ) and ( CS 2102 or CS 2103 or CS 2119 ); and machine learning equivalent to ( DS 3010 , CS 4445 , or CS 4342 ).
CS 4344/DS 4344.description: Develops language understanding and generation using NLP, deep learning and large language models, with practical system work and responsible deployment considerations.

review.rationale: NLP and language-model methods remain the central technical subject; ethics complements rather than replaces that focus.

CS 4432.name: Database Systems II
CS 4432.description: Investigates database internals, including storage and indexing, query optimization, transactions, concurrency, recovery, security and distributed operation.

review.rationale: Database infrastructure and internal execution mechanisms establish systems.

CS 4432.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit is not available for both CS4432 and CS542.
CS 4432.offering_note: Source states offering in academic years ending in even numbers; no specific term is inferred.

CS 2022/MA 2201.name: Discrete Mathematics
CS 2022/MA 2201.description: Introduces discrete structures and proof techniques through sets, relations, logic, induction, integer properties, counting and graphs.

review.rationale: Formal mathematical structures and proofs are primary, even when problems come from computing.

CS 2301.name: Systems Programming for Non-Majors
CS 2301.recommended_background: Programming experience such as found in CS 1101 , CS 1102 , CS 1004 , or CS 1005 .
CS 2301.description: Introduces C programming for non-majors with explicit memory management, pointers, stack behavior, data structures and input/output.

review.rationale: The description centers on the machine-facing programming model and memory/input-output mechanisms; its programming exercises serve that systems focus.

CS 2301.credit_restriction: Students already credited for CS2303 cannot subsequently earn CS2301 credit; the source states this direction explicitly.
CS 2301.audience_note: CS students and those preparing for upper-level CS are directed to CS2303 instead.

CS 2303.name: Systems Programming Concepts
CS 2303.recommended_background: CS 2102 , CS 2103 , or CS 2119 and/or substantial object-oriented programming experience.
CS 2303.description: Studies programming that exposes hardware storage and execution, emphasizing memory, pointers, the stack, input/output and safe C/C++ implementation.

review.rationale: Hardware-exposing memory and execution mechanisms establish systems, rather than classifying from the title alone.

CS 4120.name: Analysis of Algorithms
CS 4120.recommended_background: Algorithms ( CS 2223 or equivalent), and some knowledge of probability.
CS 4120.description: Analyzes algorithm correctness and average/worst-case behavior through sorting, string matching, graphs, dynamic programming and program profiling.

review.rationale: Algorithm design and analysis are computing foundations; probability is preparation rather than an extra course obligation.

CS 4120.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit is not available for both CS4120 and CS5084.
CS 4120.offering_note: Source states offering in academic years ending in odd numbers; no specific term is inferred.

CS 4233.name: Object-Oriented Analysis and Design
CS 4233.description: Practices object-oriented analysis through domain models, use cases and reusable design patterns applied to software-design problems.

review.rationale: Reusable software design methods establish foundations.

CS 4233.offering_note: Source states offering in academic years ending in odd numbers; no specific term is inferred.

CS 4518.name: Mobile and Ubiquitous Computing
CS 4518.recommended_background: Proficiency in programming in Java, including classes, inheritance, exceptions, interfaces, and polymorphism ( CS 2102 or equivalent).
CS 4518.description: Studies mobile and ubiquitous computing, including sensing, mobile interaction and services, device programming, performance, energy and security.

review.rationale: Mobile computing infrastructure, resource constraints and device operation provide the primary organizing subject, with application examples.

CS 4518.credit_restriction: Credit is not available for both CS403X and CS4518.

CS 4804.name: Data Visualization
CS 4804.description: Develops and evaluates data visualizations through graphical mappings, user tasks, perception, implementation and visualization tools.

review.rationale: The description combines graphical communication and user/perception evaluation with algorithm implementation; it does not establish a single dominant category.

MA 2621.name: Probability for Applications
MA 2621.description: Introduces applied probability through random variables, distributions, conditional probability, expectation and transformations.

review.rationale: Probability theory and distributional methods establish mathematics despite the application-oriented audience.

MA 2621.credit_restriction: Credit is not available for both MA2621 and MA2631.

MA 2631.name: Probability Theory
MA 2631.recommended_background: Multivariable Differential and Integral Calculus ( MA 1024 , or equivalent).
MA 2631.description: Develops probability using axioms and proofs, with random variables, distributions, expectation, transformations and limit results.

review.rationale: Explicit mathematical theory and proof establish mathematics.

MA 2631.credit_restriction: Credit is not available for both MA2631 and MA2621.

MA 1024.name: Calculus IV
MA 1024.recommended_background: MA 1023 . Although the course will make use of computers, no programming experience is assumed.
MA 1024.description: Introduces multivariable calculus through vector functions, derivatives, gradients, optimization and multiple integrals in several coordinate systems.

review.rationale: Multivariable calculus techniques are central.

MA 2210.name: Mathematical Methods in Decision Making
MA 2210.description: Uses mathematical modeling, optimization, probability and decision analysis to plan and manage complex projects.

review.rationale: Quantitative decision theory is the methodological core; engineering and actuarial cases are applications of that mathematics.

MA 2210.suggested_background: Familiarity with vectors and matrices. Although the course makes use of computers, no programming experience is assumed. Students who have received credit for CE 2010 may not receive credit for MA 2210.
MA 2210.credit_restriction: Students already credited for CE2010 cannot earn MA2210 credit.

MA 3231.name: Linear Programming
MA 3231.recommended_background: Matrices and Linear Algebra ( MA 2071 , or equivalent).
MA 3231.description: Formulates and solves linear optimization problems using simplex methods, duality and related analysis, with resource-allocation applications.

review.rationale: Optimization theory, formulation and mathematical algorithms establish mathematics.

MA 3233.name: Discrete Optimization
MA 3233.recommended_background: At least one course in graph theory, combinatorics or optimization (e.g., MA 2271 , MA 2273 or MA 3231 ).
MA 3233.description: Studies optimization on discrete structures through combinatorial methods, linear programming and algorithms, including network and matching problems.

review.rationale: Discrete optimization is explicitly treated as applied mathematics; domain examples do not change its subject.

MA 3233.offering_note: Source states offering in academic years ending in odd numbers; no specific term is inferred.

MA 4235.name: Nonlinear Optimization
MA 4235.recommended_background: Multivariable calculus at the level of MA 1024 : Calculus IV and linear algebra at the level of MA 2071 : Matrices & Linear Algebra 1.
MA 4235.description: Develops solution conditions and numerical algorithms for nonlinear constrained and unconstrained optimization.

review.rationale: Convexity, optimality conditions and optimization algorithms establish mathematics; optional stochastic gradient methods do not make the whole course AI.

MA 4237.name: Probabilistic Methods in Operations Research
MA 4237.recommended_background: Probability theory at the level of MA 2621 or MA 2631 .
MA 4237.description: Applies probabilistic methods to decisions, inventory, queues, reliability and simulation in planning and complex systems.

review.rationale: Probability-based operations-research methods determine the subject, independently of business applications.

MA 4237.offering_note: Source states offering in academic years ending in even numbers; no specific term is inferred.

CS 4032/MA 3257.name: Numerical Methods for Linear and Nonlinear Systems
CS 4032/MA 3257.recommended_background: MA 2071 . An ability to write computer programs in a scientific language is assumed.
CS 4032/MA 3257.description: Develops numerical solution methods for linear and nonlinear equations, systems and eigenvalue problems, emphasizing error analysis.

review.rationale: Numerical analysis and mathematical error reasoning are central; programming implements these methods.

MA 2251.name: Vector and Tensor Calculus
MA 2251.description: Develops vector and tensor calculus through fields, differential operations, integrals and integral theorems, illustrated by physical applications.

review.rationale: The course teaches mathematical calculus tools; physical examples are not the primary domain.

MA 2271.name: Graph Theory
MA 2271.description: Introduces graph-theoretic structures and methods, including paths, trees, cliques, planarity, duality and coloring.

review.rationale: The description explicitly emphasizes deeper mathematical graph theory, rather than only algorithm implementation.

MA 2271.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit is not available for both MA2271 and MA3271.
MA 2271.offering_note: Source states offering in academic years ending in odd numbers; no specific term is inferred.

MA 2273.name: Combinatorics
MA 2273.description: Develops combinatorial problem solving through counting, generating functions, recurrences, designs and related algorithms.

review.rationale: Combinatorial structures and mathematical techniques establish mathematics.

MA 2273.credit_restriction: Undergraduate credit is not available for both MA2273 and MA3273.
